title: Brighter Super expands indexed options following adviser demand
full_text:
Brighter Super has expanded its investment menu with indexed Australian and international share options, responding to adviser demand for more ways to tailor clients’ exposure to equity markets.
Available since 1 October, the Indexed International Shares and Indexed Australian Shares options offer passive investment strategies to members with accumulation, pension or transition to retirement pension accounts.
Both options have estimated investment fees and costs of 0.08 per cent a year and no transaction costs. Other charges, including administration fees, advice fees and insurance costs, may apply depending on members’ accounts and circumstances.
Brighter Super chief member officer Lisa Kay said the additions reflect feedback from advisers seeking more indexed investment choices.
“Advisers have told us they want greater flexibility to tailor international and Australian share exposure within their clients’ Brighter Super accounts. We listened, and these options respond directly to that feedback,” Kay said.
“These new options provide additional building blocks that advisers can combine with other Brighter Super investment options to build a portfolio suited to each client’s needs.”
The options were developed following extensive consultation with external financial adviser groups, market research conducted with Investment Trends, investment modelling, and competitor and fee analysis.
Members can combine the new options with other investments on the fund’s menu to tailor their exposure to Australian and international share markets. Brighter Super’s existing actively managed share options will remain available.
“They also give members another way to access international and Australian share markets, while our existing actively managed International Shares and Australian Shares options will remain available,” Kay said.
The Indexed International Shares option follows a weighted combination of the MSCI World Index in Australian dollars, comprising 20 per cent hedged and 80 per cent unhedged exposure.
The Indexed Australian Shares option is designed to perform in line with the S&P/ASX 300 Accumulation Index. Both investment objectives are stated before investment fees and taxes.
The additions complement Brighter Super’s existing Indexed Balanced option, which invests across a mix of asset classes, by providing separate Australian and international share exposures.
“We recognise that members and advisers have different preferences about how investments are managed,” Kay said. “Expanding the menu gives them more ways to put their investment strategy into practice within Brighter Super.”
The fund said indexed options aim to follow their respective markets through rises and falls, with lower investment fees neither indicating lower risk nor guaranteeing better returns.
Brighter Super, a member-owned fund based in Queensland, had more than 340,000 members and over $38 billion in funds under management at 30 June 2026.
